hundredIslands.heading: Discover Hundred Islands National Park
hundredIslands.body: Alaminos City is home to the Hundred Islands National Park, a protected marine reserve of over 120 limestone islands in the Lingayen Gulf — the Philippines' first national park and one of Pangasinan's most visited destinations.

history.heading: A Brief History of Alaminos City

entries.text: A Northern Zambal tribe founded the settlement of Suyang (in what is now Zaragoza, Bolinao).
Suyang's residents moved to Barrio Casborran (now Barangay Baleyadaan, Alaminos City); the community grew quickly and drew more settlers from eastern Pangasinan.
Casborran broke away from its mother town, Bolinao, and became an independent pueblo.
A dispute between the original settlers and newer migrants over politics and the economy ended in a fire that destroyed the town; survivors slowly returned to rebuild.
Rebuilding was cut short when renewed conflict forced residents to abandon the town for Nansangaan (now Barangay Inerangan).
Residents founded a new settlement on higher ground away from the coast and named it Sarapsap — today's Barangay Poblacion.
Sarapsap's growth caught the attention of Spanish Governor-General Juan Alaminos y Vivar during an official visit.
In recognition of his popularity, the town was renamed "Alaminos" in his honor.
Alaminos and eight other towns of northern Zambales were folded into Pangasinan province; Francisco Reinoso became the town's first Municipal President.
Alaminos rebuilt and its economy recovered after World War II.
The municipality was reclassified from fourth class to third class.
A further reclassification to first-class municipality followed a 338.5% rise in gross income.
President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo signed Republic Act 9025, converting Alaminos into a component city.
Voters ratified the change in a plebiscite, with 85% voting "Yes," making Alaminos Pangasinan's fourth city.

funFacts.title: Rebuilt From Disaster
funFacts.description: The town was burned down in 1758 amid a dispute between settlers, then displaced again in 1764 before finally taking root as Sarapsap — today's Poblacion — in 1766.

funFacts.title: Named Before He Was Governor-General
funFacts.description: Alaminos was named in 1872 to honor Juan Alaminos y Vivar, a year before he actually became Governor-General of the Philippines (1873–74).

funFacts.title: Home to the Philippines' First National Park
funFacts.description: The Hundred Islands, off the coast of Barangay Lucap, were declared the country's first national park by President Manuel L. Quezon in 1940.

flowchart.heading: Flowchart for Legislative Proposal
flowchart.subtitle: Step-by-step process for enacting ordinances and resolutions

fileProposal.title: File Proposed Ordinance
fileProposal.description: Submit the proposed ordinance to the Sangguniang Panlungsod for consideration.

firstReading.title: First Reading / Referral to Committee
firstReading.description: Initial reading and assignment to the relevant committee for review.

publicHearing.title: Public Hearing / Committee Action
publicHearing.description: Committee conducts a public hearing and deliberates on the proposed ordinance.

committeeReport.title: Committee Report
committeeReport.description: Committee submits its findings and recommendations to the Sangguniang Panlungsod.

secondReading.title: Second Reading
secondReading.description: Detailed discussion and debate on the proposed ordinance.

thirdReading.title: Third and Final Reading
thirdReading.description: Final voting on the proposed ordinance by the Sangguniang Panlungsod.

mayorApproval.title: 10-Day Mayor's Approval
mayorApproval.description: The City Mayor reviews and approves the enacted ordinance within 10 days.

spSubmission.title: 3-Day Submission to SP
spSubmission.description: The approved ordinance is submitted to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for review within 3 days.

spReview.title: SP Review Period
spReview.description: 60-day review period for appropriation ordinances; 30-day review for others.

posting.title: Posting / Publication
posting.description: Public posting and publication of the approved ordinance.

implementation.title: Implementation
implementation.description: The ordinance takes effect and is enforced within the city.

fileProposal.title: File Proposed Resolution
fileProposal.description: Submit the proposed resolution to the Sangguniang Panlungsod.

sessionAgenda.title: Inclusion in Session Agenda
sessionAgenda.description: The resolution is scheduled for inclusion in a Sangguniang Panlungsod session.

committeeApproval.title: Committee Meeting / Approval
committeeApproval.description: Committee reviews and approves the proposed resolution.

finalDraft.title: Final Draft Printing
finalDraft.description: Legislative staff prepares and prints the final draft of the resolution.

officialSigning.title: Official Signing
officialSigning.description: The Secretary to the Sanggunian and the Presiding Officer sign the resolution.

postingTransmittal.title: Posting / Transmittal
postingTransmittal.description: The resolution is posted publicly and transmitted to concerned parties.

publicParticipation.title: Public Participation

transparency.title: Transparency

about.missionBody: BetterAlaminosCity.org is a volunteer-run civic project. It is not an official website of the Alaminos City government — it aggregates publicly available information about city services, offices, and ordinances to make them easier to find. Content is drawn from official government sources where available and clearly marked as a placeholder where it isn't yet verified.
about.contributeBody: This project is open source and welcomes contributions from developers, translators, and residents who want to help verify content. Read the contributing guide and code of conduct before opening a pull request.
about.techStackBody: Built with React Router, the Kapwa civic design system, and i18next for English/Filipino translation, this site is fully open source under the MIT license and maintained by volunteers — not the Alaminos City government.

privacy.heading: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: BetterAlaminosCity.org respects your privacy. This policy explains what little information this site handles, in line with the Philippines' Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173).
privacy.noAccountsHeading: We Don't Ask You to Create an Account
privacy.noAccountsBody: This site has no logins, accounts, or forms that collect personal information. You can browse every page, service listing, and document without providing any personal data.
privacy.serverLogsBody: Like virtually all websites, this site is served through a hosting provider (Vercel) that automatically logs standard technical data for every visit — such as IP address, browser type, and pages requested — for security and reliability purposes. BetterAlaminosCity.org does not separately collect, analyze, or sell this data, and this site does not run its own analytics or advertising trackers.
privacy.noSensitiveDataBody: We do not collect government IDs, health records, financial information, or any other sensitive personal information through this site.
privacy.contactBody: This project doesn't operate a monitored email inbox. If you reach out — for example, to report an error or suggest a correction — you'll do so by opening an issue on GitHub.
privacy.contactFollowUp: Anything you post there is public and governed by GitHub's own Privacy Statement, not this policy.
privacy.cookiesBody: This site does not set tracking or advertising cookies.
privacy.rightsHeading: Your Rights Under the Data Privacy Act
privacy.rightsBody: Because this site collects no personal information directly, there is no personal data for us to hold, correct, or delete on your behalf. If you have concerns about data handled by our hosting provider, you may also contact the National Privacy Commission.
privacy.changesBody: This policy may be updated as the site evolves — for example, if a future feature introduces forms or accounts, this page will be updated to describe exactly what's collected and why.
privacy.contactFooterBody: Questions about this policy can be raised on GitHub.

accessibility.heading: Accessibility
accessibility.intro: BetterAlaminosCity.org aims to be usable by everyone, including residents using assistive technology. We treat accessibility as an ongoing responsibility, not a one-time checklist.
accessibility.targetBody: We design this site to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA. This is a target we build toward, not a certified or independently audited conformance claim — no formal accessibility audit of this site has been conducted yet.
accessibility.targetLinkLabel: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA
accessibility.featuresBody: Semantic HTML headings and landmarks throughout the site · ARIA labels on interactive controls like the navigation menu and language switcher · a responsive layout that works from mobile screens up to desktop · full bilingual support in English and Filipino, so residents can read content in whichever language they're more comfortable with.
accessibility.limitationsBody: Some linked source documents — such as the Citizen's Charter PDF and scanned ordinances/resolutions — are published by the city government in formats that may not be fully accessible to screen readers; we can't modify documents we don't originate. Some pages are still being verified against official sources and may contain incomplete content.
accessibility.feedbackBody: If you run into an accessibility barrier anywhere on this site, please let us know by opening an issue describing the page and the problem you encountered.
accessibility.techBody: This site is built with React Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and i18next, and is fully open source under the MIT License.

general.heading: General
general.hoursQuestion: What are City Hall's office hours?
general.hoursAnswer: City Hall (Quezon Avenue, Poblacion, Alaminos City) is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
general.directoryQuestion: Is there a directory of office contact numbers?
general.directoryAnswer: Not yet a general one — most office listings on this site don't have public contact numbers verified. For emergencies, see the Emergency Hotlines section on the homepage. For office locations and what each one handles, see the Government directory.
general.onlineQuestion: Can I complete transactions online, or do I need to go in person?
general.onlineAnswer: It depends on the service. Some, like business permit applications and renewals, can be started online through the city's eLGU/eBOSS portal or the eGOV PH mobile app, in addition to the in-person option. Others, like most civil registry document requests, are handled in person at the relevant office. Check the specific service directory for each transaction's requirements.

documents.heading: Certificates & Documents
documents.birthCertQuestion: How long does it take to get a birth certificate?
documents.birthCertAnswer: It depends on what you're requesting. A certified photocopy of an existing birth record on file with the Local Civil Registrar typically takes about 35 minutes to process; the same request made online through eLGU takes about 45 minutes. Registering a new birth on time (not a copy request) takes about 45 minutes to process. See the Civil Registry & Vital Records services category for full details.
documents.birthCertLinkLabel: Browse Civil Registry & Vital Records services
documents.representativeQuestion: Can someone else request a document on my behalf?
documents.representativeAnswer: Yes. Your representative will need a valid government-issued ID for both of you, plus a notarized Special Power of Attorney or Authorization Letter. If the authorization was sent by email or messenger, a printed copy with a photo of you holding the original authorization and your ID is also required.
documents.psaQuestion: What's the difference between a PSA copy and a local civil registrar copy?
documents.psaAnswer: The Local Civil Registrar's Office can issue certified photocopies of records it holds directly. Separately, the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) offers copies of records already on file nationally through its online Serbilis Outlets, which this office can also help you request. Which one you need depends on the purpose of the document — check with the Civil Registrar's Office if you're unsure.

business.heading: Business & Permits
business.newBusinessQuestion: What do I need to register a new business?
business.newBusinessAnswer: Generally: a Barangay Clearance, a Community Tax Certificate, and proof of business registration — a DTI Certificate of Registration for a sole proprietorship, or an SEC registration with Articles of Incorporation for a corporation or partnership. The full requirement list (and the online eBOSS alternative) is on the Business services page.

payments.heading: Payments & Fees
payments.paymentMethodsQuestion: How do I pay city fees?
payments.paymentMethodsAnswer: If you're using the online eBOSS business permit process, payment is made through QR Ph. For in-person transactions, fees are paid at the City Treasurer's Office; this site doesn't yet have verified information on which payment methods (cash, card, e-wallet) are accepted onsite — confirm with the Treasurer's Office directly.
payments.propertyTaxQuestion: When is real property tax due?
payments.propertyTaxAnswer: Real property tax is generally due quarterly, and a discount is typically available if you pay the full year in one go. Exact deadlines and rates are published annually by the City Treasurer's Office.

social.heading: Social Services
social.seniorIdQuestion: What do I need to apply for a Senior Citizen ID?
social.seniorIdAnswer: A photocopy of your birth certificate, a valid ID, and an accomplished Personal Information Sheet from the Senior Citizen's Office. There's no fee. See the Social Welfare services category for the full process.
